reference_guided_design.owner_intent: The owner confirmed that users should be able to redesign any part of the desktop workbench with embedded AI, including replacing its original regions and visual structure or starting from scratch. Users describe the result they want in their own words or choose a screenshot or reference URL. Mobbin and Dribbble are examples. Any visible detail, a composition spanning former regions, or the entire workbench can be the target. Panels and groupings are possible outcomes of the design.
reference_guided_design.visual_reference: Interpret an accessible reference for visual cues such as hierarchy, spacing, typography and composition, then express the result as an editable ScopeHub layout. Keep the user's current model route and scoped disclosure. If the page is inaccessible or the model cannot view it, offer a user-selected screenshot when image input is supported or ask for a text description.
reference_guided_design.composition: The proposal uses editable descriptions that can combine fields, images, text, cards, rows and split lists within or across existing regions. These are examples of what users can compose. Visual edits govern presentation. Data and actions come from independently available capabilities and existing grants, and feed records come from the configured service. Preserve record identity, attribution and links across layout changes and apply the same grouping rules to new records on refresh.
reference_guided_design.editing_scope: Manual and AI edits share a saved, editable workbench with preview and undo. A local edit preserves composition and bindings outside its requested scope, even when the edit spans former regions. A whole-workbench edit can replace the original arrangement. Global settings, credentials and native permission dialogs stay outside workbench customization.

illustrative_acceptance.given: A synthetic, authorized information feed supplies item IDs, headlines, source names and links, publication times and an optional image. The initial workbench shows a Top News list beside another widget.
illustrative_acceptance.actions: Restyle only the list as image cards. Keep a text card for an item with no image. Split the same feed into two independently placed views, for example today's and earlier headlines using the displayed time zone. Then use a reference to rearrange the whole workbench.
illustrative_acceptance.observations_to_verify: The local edit preserves the neighboring widget. Every original item appears once across the two time groups with its source, time and link intact. A new matching item appears under the same rule on refresh. Undo restores the prior presentation and retains the data. Saving and reopening restores the revised composition and rechecks its bindings.

reference_guided_design.status: Confirmed owner intent with a proposed implementation and prospective acceptance example. The news example requires a separately configured and granted information service. Desktop reference ingestion, multimodal interpretation and the proposed feed presentation still require implementation and validation.

current_scope.v1: The contract specifies one main instrument chart and declarative customization. ScopeHub already saves and restores named single-chart layouts. The current price display switches between candles and a close-price line, with volume below. Indicator series render as price overlays or in separate panes appended after volume.
current_scope.M2-012: Planned current-contract work composes built-in widgets around the single main chart, starting with an inspection table. It covers compatible authorized local and API bindings, linked or independent selections, arrangement and restore.
current_scope.M2-003: Planned later work evaluates isolated user-authored panels only when a concrete need exceeds declarative bindings. Runtime execution would require a separate decision.

recommendations.starting_points: Offer an editable TradingView-inspired default and a genuinely blank starting point. Users can replace the default composition or keep any pieces they want while editing directly or with AI. Keep a workspace menu reachable for starting a composition or restoring the default.
recommendations.workspace: Let users create, combine, split, move and resize parts of the workbench in a composition of their choosing. OpenBB Workspace offers examples of arrangement and resizing interactions. Relative sizing can adapt the composition to window changes, with snapping or docking as optional aids. Bind visual elements to compatible authorized data and let users link or independently choose selections.
recommendations.chart: The target experience includes showing candles and a close-price line simultaneously, side by side, stacked or in other user-chosen positions, with volume, indicators or other authorized data placed anywhere relative to them. These are examples. Use compatible axes for overlays and shared time alignment where useful, with independent scales or units as needed. Users can link selections or choose independent symbols, timeframes and viewports. Daily bars and opening or closing auction records alone cannot supply a continuous intraday price series.
recommendations.appearance: Make typography, colors, line styles, spacing and proportions editable as part of the composition. Keep source attribution, freshness and action confirmations accessible across custom layouts.
recommendations.editing_and_recovery: Use one versioned layout for manual and AI edits through the shared operation registry. Use stable identities for editable elements and store their relationships and positions. Preview and undo scoped or whole-workbench changes. Save named layouts and recover the last committed revision after interruption. On reopen, recheck source grants and preserve the intended placement when data is unavailable.
recommendations.boundaries: Keep source grants separate from layout references and attach immutable indicator results by version. The controlled desktop renderer interprets the editable layout. Designs beyond the current rendering vocabulary may need new rendering support or a separately reviewed isolated extension. Arbitrary code and foreign pages stay outside the main WebView.

prospective_chart_story: With authorized bars and a computed indicator, I ask the embedded AI to show candles on the left and the close-price line on the right at the same time, with volume below both. I then show a reference for stacking the line above candles. I ask it to move volume out of the former chart region into a shared band across the workbench and place the indicator between the two price plots. I can link both plots to one instrument and timeframe or pin an independent selection or timeframe where the source supports it. I preview the edit, undo to recover the side-by-side arrangement, then reapply and save the stacked design. On reopen I verify placement, selection links and authorized data bindings.

observed_library_probe.setup: Headless Chromium with lightweight-charts 5.2.1 and 65 synthetic one-minute bars. The visible logical range was 18..48.
observed_library_probe.result: A test line moved from below volume to between price and volume. Its pane measured 86 px. Price and volume values and the logical range stayed the same. Removing the line restored the original price and volume order.
observed_library_probe.scope: Chart library only. Native UI, model interaction and persistence still require product validation.

first_proposed_demonstration: With a frozen desktop sample, use manual controls and an embedded AI request to preview and place the same existing computed indicator between candles and volume. Resize its pane, undo the resize and placement, then reapply, save the named layout and reopen it. Check that order and size restore and that values, symbol selections, visible range and source authorization stay the same throughout.
open_release_scope: The owner confirmed the target experience. First-release timing remains open for simultaneous price presentations, restructuring across former regions, ordered pane editing, reference-guided design from scratch and a genuinely blank start with chart-free saved layouts. The current V1 contract specifies a single main chart.
